title: Write for a 5th grader: Sam Parr's copywriting rule for making people keep reading
summary: A 2015 essay on writing that gets people to act. Sam's core rule: write like you're talking to a 5th grader, using short words, short sentences, and short paragraphs so each sentence earns the next. He also lists the books, courses, and tools he used to study persuasion.

principles.text: Write as if to a 5th grader: one or two syllable words, short sentences, short paragraphs.
principles.quote: whenever you write, act like you’re writing to a 5th grader.

principles.text: Each sentence has one job: get the reader to read the next sentence.
principles.quote: the point of the first sentence is to get you to read the second sentence. And the point of the second sentence is to get you to read the third sentence.

principles.text: Good copy creates a slippery slope where the reader melts into the text.
principles.quote: A well written email, blog post, or book creates a slippery slope. The reader melts away into the copy.

principles.text: You don't need to be a great writer; studying human psychology is what beats most people.
principles.quote: I don’t consider myself a great writer. My grammar sucks. I am notorious for typos. But I am better than most.

principles.text: Learn persuasion by studying what makes humans tick, not just grammar.
principles.quote: Because I study humans and what makes them tick.

principles.text: Use a readability tool like Hemingway App and aim for a 5th grade level while writing.
principles.quote: Use Hemingway App while writing. Aim for a 5th grade level.
